title: CORS headers and preflight in node:http
when: A page on one origin calls an API on another (other port or domain) and requests fail with a CORS error, or the API must allow chosen sites.
inputs: methods and headers the client sends
prompt:
Goal: An API that answers preflight correctly and allows only the listed origins, methods and headers.
Steps:
1. Parse ALLOWED_ORIGINS from config (comma list such as http://localhost:5500) into a Set.
2. If req.headers.origin is in the Set, set access-control-allow-origin to that exact origin plus vary: Origin.
3. OPTIONS preflight: 204 with access-control-allow-methods, access-control-allow-headers (content-type, authorization) and access-control-max-age: 600, without running the route.
4. Only when cookies or auth cross origins add access-control-allow-credentials: true; it never works with a * origin.
5. List response headers the client reads in access-control-expose-headers (Location).
6. Unknown origins get no CORS headers; the browser blocks them.
Quality bar:
- Allowed sites work for every method the API offers.
- Same origin requests without Origin keep working.
- Error responses carry CORS headers too, so clients can read them.
Pitfalls:
- A * origin on an API that uses cookies.
- Echoing any Origin back unchecked.
- No OPTIONS route, so preflight gets 404 or 405.
Verify:
- [ ] OPTIONS returns 204 with methods and headers.
- [ ] Origins are checked against the Set.
- [ ] vary: Origin is set.
- [ ] Unknown routes still return 404.
Output: cors.mjs exporting applyCors(req, res), which returns true after answering a preflight; called first in server.mjs.

examples.input: meu front em localhost:5500 dá erro de CORS chamando a API na 3000
examples.output: applyCors with an allow list, 204 preflight, vary Origin, credentials only when needed
